correctness.rationale: Every positive Q-gap has unique Sylvester coordinates; PF corresponds to Pareto minimal congruent lattice points. Bound coordinates by p and use a,b>=2p+1, gcd(ab,p)=1 to identify a permutation. The record-drop pigeonhole inequality proves at least p-3N-1>=1 adjacent one-step record transition, forcing a/b=1 modulo p. The residue equivalence, empty p-1 case, and witnesses follow. Independent Apéry Dijkstra tests 12,343 triples, record checks 4,351 and modular census 3,491,756 comparisons passed. Finite checks are not used to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: The type of a numerical semigroup is a natural central invariant. This result gives the sharp forbidden value immediately below the attainable maximum and describes exactly the unique upper-spectrum residue classes over arbitrary (even composite) moduli, with a new extremal combinatorial argument. It is not a low-dimensional computer table or a rebranding of an individual PF algorithm.
